props.gloss_en: Rav Huna: if he slept in his fast [continued it through the night], he does not pray the fast prayer [the next morning]
Rav Yosef's first alternative: Rav Huna holds one does not fast for hours
Rav Yosef's second alternative: one does fast for hours, but one who fasts for hours does not pray the fast prayer
one fasts for hours -- a fast of some hours counts as a fast
and one who fasts for hours prays the fast prayer
Abaye: here it differs, for there are night hours he did not accept upon himself at the outset
the jars of gentiles, after twelve months, are permitted
Moses served all seven days of the miluim in a white cloak
Rav Kahana's version: in a white cloak that has no hem
Rav Chisda: the ruling that one fasts for hours holds provided he tasted nothing until evening
Rav Chisda: any fast on which the sun has not set is not called a fast
the baraita: the men of the [priestly] watch fast and do not complete [the fast]
there it is merely to afflict oneself [not a fast proper]
R' Elazar b. R' Tzadok: once 9 Av fell on Shabbat, we postponed it past Shabbat, fasted on it and did not complete it, because it is our [family's] festival
R' Yochanan: I shall be fasting until I come to my house
there he did it to excuse himself from the Nasi's household
Shmuel: any fast not accepted while it was still day is not called a fast
(asked: and if he sat [fasting] anyway, what is he?) Rabba bar Sheila: he is like a bellows full of air
Rav: one accepts the fast at [the time of] mincha
Shmuel: one accepts the fast in the mincha prayer
Megillat Taanit: any person who has taken upon himself beforehand [a fast on one of these days] -- yeisar (the word whose reading is disputed)
the reading ייסר: he binds himself [to the fast] in his prayer
the reading יאסר: he is forbidden [to fast on those days]
Megillat Taanit: an individual who vowed Mondays and Thursdays all year, and the Megilla's festivals fell on them -- if his vow preceded our decree, his vow annuls our decree
and if our decree preceded his vow, our decree annuls his vow
Rebbi: [on the night before a fast] one eats and drinks until dawn
R' Elazar b. R' Shimon: until the cock's crow
Abaye: they taught this only where he has not finished his meal; once he has finished his meal he does not eat
the baraita: [if] he finished and rose -- he may eat
Rava (איכא דאמרי): they taught this only where he did not sleep; if he slept he does not eat
the baraita: [if] he slept and rose -- he may eat
(asked: what is dozing?) Rav Ashi: asleep and not asleep, awake and not awake -- called, he answers; he cannot give a reasoned reply; reminded, he remembers
Rav: an individual who accepted a fast is forbidden to wear shoes
Rav's ground: we fear that perhaps he accepted a communal fast
(asked: how should he act?) Rabba bar Rav Sheila: let him say thus -- 'tomorrow I shall be before You in an individual's fast'
the rabbanan to Rav Sheshet: we see rabbanan who wear their shoes and come to the fast-house
Abaye [and Rava] wore [their shoes] on the upper
[Abaye and] Rava wore [their shoes] on the upper
Mareimar [and Mar Zutra] switched right [shoe] to left and left to right
[Mareimar and] Mar Zutra switched right [shoe] to left and left to right
the rabbanan of Rav Ashi's house went out [in their shoes] in their usual way
Shmuel: there is no communal fast in Bavel except the Ninth of Av alone (gloss-only: a quantified 'only' -- see header)
Rav: a person borrows his fast and repays [it]
Shmuel (as Rav Yehuda reports): did he accept a vow, that he cannot but repay? he accepted [only] to afflict himself
if he is able, he afflicts himself; if he is not able, he does not
Shmuel (איכא דאמרי): obvious! let it be no more than a vow -- may one not repay a vow tomorrow or another day?
Rav Yehoshua b. Rav Idi: I am sitting in a fast
Rav Yehoshua b. Rav Idi: it is a dream fast
Rav: a fast is good for a dream as fire is for chaff
Rav Chisda: and on that [very] day
Rav Yosef: even on Shabbat [one fasts for a dream]
(asked: what is his remedy [for fasting on Shabbat]?) let him sit a fast for the fast
